title: L0 Capstone: All About You
story: You've made it! From printing your first message to building loops and making decisions, you've mastered the basics of programming. Now it's time to show off everything you know in one big capstone project — a complete profile all about YOU, built from every concept in Level 0.
why: The best way to prove you've learned something is to build something with it. This capstone combines printing, variables, strings, math, decisions, and loops into one program that's uniquely yours.
analogy: A capstone project is like the final song at a concert — it brings together every instrument and melody you've practiced, playing them all at once to create something bigger than any single part.
try_it: Add a section about your hobbies using a for loop: create a list of your hobbies like [\"soccer\", \"drawing\", \"coding\"] and print each one with \"I love \" before it. Then add a grade-checking section using elif. Can you also calculate your age in dog years and print it? Make this profile 100% YOU!
tips: Build one section at a time — write the name section, test it, then add age, then math, and so on.
Use descriptive variable names so anyone reading your code knows what each one holds.
Break long outputs into smaller `io.print` calls to stay on one line, or use `io.println` for line breaks.
This is YOUR program — customize every variable, add your own sections, and make it show off who you are.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to declare types for math variables: `let age = 14;` works, but `let age: Int = 14;` is clearer about intent.
Mixing up `io.print` and `io.println` — `io.print` keeps you on the same line, `io.println` adds a new line after.
Using `let` for the while loop counter: you need `var` because the count needs to change inside the loop.
Putting all the code in one giant block without testing — if something breaks, it's harder to find. Test section by section!
